question.text: 'Aravalli Growth Fund III', a Category II AIF, is nearing its Final Close. What is the maximum number of investors permitted in the scheme under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: 1,000 investors per scheme (accredited investors excluded from the count under the 2025 amendment)
49 investors per scheme, consistent with Companies Act private placement limits

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 504 of the workbook states that no scheme of an AIF shall have more than 1,000 investors, with accredited investors excluded from this count. The same page also notes that for AIFs structured as a Company, the Companies Act private-placement limit applies separately. The Trap: 200 is the Companies Act private-placement / Angel Fund-style limit, 49 is an outdated private-placement number, and 'unlimited' is wrong because a ceiling does exist. Note: Accredited investors are excluded while counting the 1,000-investor scheme cap, so an accredited-investor-heavy scheme can have more than 1,000 total investors as long as the non-accredited count stays within the cap.
